html:
Hambantota Port is a deep-water port on the south coast of Sri Lanka, opened in 2010 and built mostly with loans from China.

It was a pet project of President Mahinda Rajapaksa, whose home district it is. Few ships came, and the loans were hard to repay. In 2017 the government leased the port for 99 years to a Chinese state company for about 1.1 billion US dollars.

Critics called it a debt trap and a sign of Belt and Road power next to India; others point out that Chinese loans were a small share of the island's debt. The debts of those years came due in the crisis of 2022, when Sri Lanka defaulted for the first time. The port sits on the main sea route between the Suez Canal and the Strait of Malacca.
sum: Hambantota Port is a deep-water port on the south coast of Sri Lanka, opened in 2010 and built mostly with loans from China.
